html:
Land diving, naghol, is an old rite of south Pentecost island in which men jump from tall wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles. It is held each year at the yam harvest, from about April to June.

The vines are cut to stop the diver just as his head brushes the ground, which is said to bless the yam crop. Boys first jump from low platforms, men from the top, as a test of courage.

Film of the dives inspired the first modern bungee jumps in England in 1979. Pentecost villages now control filming and tourist visits, and the rite remains a mark of kastom, the customs Vanuatu defends. See also kava and Roi Mata.
